old: While the party rests, it may buy back one spark. Every character pays four *souls* of their own to the supply, and the spark dial is turned up by one. If any character holds fewer than four souls, the party cannot buy the spark, because souls cannot be transferred or pooled (see §7.6).

The cost is four *souls* for each character in the party, paid to the supply by any combination of the characters, and the spark dial is turned up by one. The spark is not bought unless the full cost is paid. This cost and the cost of the *bonfire ascetic* are the only costs that the characters pay together (see §18.7); souls are never passed from one character to another (see §7.6).

evidence: Official 2017 campaign rules: sparks bought 'at a cost of 2 souls per character in the group' from the shared soul cache (DS-Core-Rules-lores.txt 1601-1606); source manuscript and §18.7: the ascetic is paid 'from any combination of character contributions'.

In campaign play the dial's maximum is one more than its starting value and a *spark* may be bought back for *souls* (see §18.3).
new: **Spark.** The *bonfire*'s charges, tracked on the spark dial. The party begins with six minus the number of characters, gains one for each boss defeated, and spends one each time the characters rest at the *bonfire* (see §7.4). If the characters are required to rest while the dial shows zero, the players lose the game (see §7.1). In campaign play the dial's maximum is one more than its starting value, to a limit of five, and the party may buy back a *spark* for four *souls* for each character (see §18.3).

new: **Fog gate.** The token that marks the doorway of a boss encounter. A boss encounter begins when the characters pass through it. new:
## 19.4 The Gauntlet

This campaign requires the core set and the Phantoms expansion. The party may add the *encounter cards* of any other expansion.

The party does not place *invader tokens* during this campaign (see §12.2). An *encounter* that lists an *invader* includes that invader every time the characters enter that encounter, until the invader is killed. A listed invader that has been killed does not appear again. The invader is fought under the invader rules (see §12.2), except that an invader that vanishes, or whose encounter is *failed*, returns the next time the characters enter that encounter.
rationale: The Gauntlet's own rule differs from Ambush Lies Ahead: each invader must be beaten, which is the point of the campaign.
evidence: DS-Phantoms-Rules-lores.txt 636-640: 'Unlike the standard invader rules or other campaign encounters, when an encounter lists an invader, that invader is part of the encounter every time the party enters that encounter until the invader is defeated.'

old: Every *boss* encounter of this campaign, including the *mini-boss* encounter, is fought on a *mega-boss game board*. After Section One is completed, the party plays Section Two A, Section Two B, and Section Two C in the order it chooses. The players win the campaign when all three are completed.
new:
Every *boss* encounter of this campaign, including the *mini-boss* encounter, is fought on a *mega-boss game board*. The Asylum Demon is fought on the mega-boss side of the Asylum Demon expansion's game board (see §17.3). When Section One is completed, every character gains 16 *souls* in addition to the boss reward (see §7.6). The party then plays Section Two A, Section Two B, and Section Two C in the order it chooses, and sets up each of them when the section before it is completed (see §18.1, Section Setup). The players win the campaign when all three are completed.

The party may replace the mega-boss of any of these three sections with another mega-boss it owns, and may add further sections of the same form. Each such section uses the game board and the Level 4 encounter cards of its own mega-boss.
rationale: Restores the campaign's own soul grant, names the board for the mini-boss, and says when each of the three free-order sections is set up.
evidence: Official Manus booklet, Big Game Hunting: 'When the party successfully defeats Section 1, each character gains 16 souls in addition to the souls they would gain normally'; 'each boss fight takes place on a mega boss tile, even the mini boss fight'; 'Players are also welcome to play Big Game Hunting with additional mega bosses or with alternative mega bosses'.
